results.quote: Six stem segments: 1 at the root collar, 6 at the crown.
Each holds whole units of sap (non-negativity is not stated)
Holding volume: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
all start QUIET. ... Starting sap: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Stem limit: 38 ... Everything transpired or respired goes on the loss tally, starting at 0.
each runs these five steps in order, every step finished on all segments before the next.
Uptake: add each segment's uptake for the cycle; it may go over its holding volume.
work segments 1 to 6 in turn. Sap over a segment's holding volume goes up the xylem into the next segment toward the crown, leaving that segment full
What arrives counts before that segment is worked, so excess can carry several segments up.
segment 6's excess is transpired.
State check, on sap after push-up: QUIET at or above its upper mark turns SINK-ACTIVE
SINK-ACTIVE at or below its lower mark turns QUIET
otherwise, including between the marks, the state stays. Log each change as (cycle, position, before, after).
first, from sap and states as they stand, work out all six amounts, rounded down ... Then each gives its amount, all at once.
QUIET a quarter ... QUIET sap is respired.
SINK-ACTIVE half ... SINK-ACTIVE sap goes down the phloem into the next segment toward the root ... from segment 1 it goes on the tally.
Then each gives its amount, all at once. ... which may then sit over holding volume until next cycle's push-up, or for good after cycle 5
Leaf-drop: if the six total strictly above 38
halve every segment, rounded down, the removed sap transpired; log the cycle.

end sap per segment, positions 1 to 6; end states, 1 to 6; every state change as (cycle, position, before, after); the cycles leaf-drop fired; the loss tally; and the balance check: starting sap plus all uptake equals end sap plus loss tally.
